{"id": "ab4aa4e9-bc00-463b-9797-4e3c4d646d39", "role": "user", "content": [{"id": "tooluse_f2Zt35NnuBUbbkNiHDeUT3", "content": "[{'text': '# Troubleshoot: Amazon EBS cost and billing\\n\\n## When this path applies\\n\\n- \"Why did my EBS bill go up?\", unexplained Amazon EBS charges, a cost forecast\\n- Idle, unattached or over-provisioned volumes\\n- Snapshot cost growth, Recycle Bin retention cost\\n- Questions about the Amazon EBS pricing model\\n\\n## Procedure\\n\\n1. **Get the cost trend.** AWS Cost Explorer `GetCostAndUsage`, monthly for the last several months and daily for the month that changed, grouped by `USAGE_TYPE`. Amazon EBS charges appear under the \"EC2 - Other\" service in Cost Explorer; confirm this with `GetDimensionValues` for `SERVICE` in the account.\\n2. **List the account\\'s usage types.** `GetDimensionValues` for `USAGE_TYPE` in the period. Do not trust a hardcoded list. Classify each Amazon EBS usage type by its name:\\n   - volume storage (names containing `VolumeUsage`)\\n   - provisioned IOPS (names containing `IOPS`)\\n   - provisioned throughput (names containing `Throughput`)\\n   - snapshots (names containing `Snapshot`)\\n3. **Break the change into components.** Report the change in storage, provisioned IOPS above the included baseline, provisioned throughput above the included baseline, and snapshots, using the account\\'s own Cost Explorer amounts. These include the account\\'s discounts and pricing agreements, so never replace them with list prices.\\n4. **Explain the gp3 model when gp3 is involved.** gp3 includes 3,000 IOPS and 125 MiB/s at any size. Only IOPS above 3,000 and throughput above 125 MiB/s are billed as provisioned performance. Link the pricing page; do not type a price.\\n5. **Find what changed.**\\n   - `DescribeVolumesModifications` for every volume: original and target size, type, IOPS and throughput, with start time. This record is not bound by AWS CloudTrail retention.\\n   - `DescribeVolumes` `CreateTime` for new volumes, and `status=available` for unattached volumes.\\n   - Volume type changes (for example gp2 to gp3, or gp3 to io2) from the modification record.\\n   - Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager `GetLifecyclePolicies` and AWS Backup `ListBackupPlans` for policies that create or retain snapshots.\\n   - Recycle Bin `ListRules`: resources in Recycle Bin are still billed during retention.\\n   - AWS CloudTrail `LookupEvents` is optional, only if available, to find who made a change. If it is denied or empty, write a Gap and continue.\\n6. **Right-sizing check** for volumes with provisioned performance.\\n   - Measured IOPS and MiB/s over a representative window (`VolumeAvgIOPS` / `VolumeAvgThroughput` with `VolumeId` and `InstanceId`, or the Sum-based math in [data-collection.md](data-collection.md)) against provisioned values.\\n   - Provisioned performance above what the attached instance\\'s EBS baseline can deliver.\\n   - AWS Compute Optimizer `GetEBSVolumeRecommendations` if enabled (optional).\\n7. **Separate findings.** Posture issues seen during the check (unencrypted volumes, untagged volumes, no backup coverage, no alarms) go under Separate findings with a suggestion to run Review mode ([review-operational.md](review-operational.md)).\\n\\n## Decision rules\\n\\n- The Answer names the component and the resource that drove the change, with the date from the modification record or `CreateTime`.\\n- Snapshot savings are an upper bound because snapshots are incremental.\\n- A volume with provisioned performance far above measured demand or above the instance baseline is a right-sizing candidate. Do not apply a fixed percentage rule; show the measured and provisioned values and let the operator decide.\\n\\n## What to report\\n\\nThe verdict template in [finding-logic.md](finding-logic.md). Evidence is a table of components (storage, IOPS, throughput, snapshots) with the account\\'s own amounts for the two periods compared, and the change records that explain each. Binding layer is \"Not applicable\". Recommendation lists right-sizing, deletion or type-change proposals with exact parameters and cost direction.\\n\\n## Safety rules\\n\\n- This path is read-only.\\n- Deleting volumes or snapshots, changing volume types and lowering IOPS or throughput are proposals for a directed action approved on the approval card. Each proposal names the volume, the exact parameters, the cost direction and the rollback. For deletions, recommend a snapshot first and say whether a Recycle Bin rule will catch it.\\n- Never type a price. Use the account\\'s Cost Explorer amounts and link the pricing page.\\n\\n## Sources\\n\\n- Amazon EBS pricing: https://aws.amazon.com/ebs/pricing/\\n- gp3 included performance: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/general-purpose.html\\n- Monitoring volume modifications: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/monitoring-volume-modifications.html\\n- Snapshots (incremental): https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/ebs-snapshots.html\\n- Recycle Bin: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/recycle-bin.html\\n- Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/snapshot-lifecycle.html\\n- AWS Backup resource assignment: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/aws-backup/latest/devguide/assigning-resources.html\\n'}]", "status": "success", "type": "tool_result"}, {"id": "tooluse_YmrceAPhdCD4dl2kmMLVD4", "content": "[{'text': '# Data collection: read-only APIs, metric math, errors and fallbacks\\n\\nLoad this file on every request. Every value in a verdict or a review comes from one of these calls. Tags are used for naming only, never as the source of a configuration value.\\n\\n## Read-only API allowlist\\n\\n| Service | APIs |\\n|---|---|\\n| Amazon EC2 | `DescribeVolumes`, `DescribeVolumeStatus`, `DescribeVolumesModifications`, `DescribeVolumeAttribute`, `DescribeInstances`, `DescribeInstanceTypes`, `DescribeInstanceAttribute`, `DescribeSnapshots`, `DescribeSnapshotAttribute`, `DescribeImages`, `DescribeFastSnapshotRestores`, `GetEbsEncryptionByDefault`, `GetEbsDefaultKmsKeyId`, `GetSnapshotBlockPublicAccessState`, `DescribeLockedSnapshots` |\\n| Amazon CloudWatch | `DescribeAlarms`, `DescribeAlarmHistory`, `GetMetricData`, `ListMetrics` |\\n| Service Quotas | `ListServiceQuotas`, `GetServiceQuota`, `GetAWSDefaultServiceQuota`, `ListRequestedServiceQuotaChangeHistoryByQuota` |\\n| Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager | `GetLifecyclePolicies`, `GetLifecyclePolicy` |\\n| Recycle Bin | `ListRules`, `GetRule` |\\n| AWS Backup | `ListBackupPlans`, `ListBackupSelections`, `GetBackupSelection`, `ListRecoveryPointsByResource` (always with `ManagedByAWSBackupOnly` set to true; without it the call also returns snapshots AWS Backup did not create), `ListProtectedResources` |\\n| AWS KMS | `DescribeKey`, `GetKeyPolicy`, `ListGrants` |\\n| AWS Cost Explorer | `GetCostAndUsage`, `GetDimensionValues` |\\n| AWS FIS | `ListExperiments`, `GetExperiment` |\\n| AWS Health | `DescribeEvents` |\\n| AWS Compute Optimizer (optional) | `GetEBSVolumeRecommendations` |\\n| AWS CloudTrail (optional) | `LookupEvents`. This call is optional. If it is denied or returns nothing, record a Gap and continue. Never make it a required step |\\n\\nNothing outside this list is called by the skill on its own. Mutating calls are proposals (see SKILL.md Critical rules).\\n\\n## Metric rules\\n\\nAWS/EBS publishes 1-minute data.\\n\\n| Namespace | Metrics | Dimensions |\\n|---|---|---|\\n| AWS/EBS | `VolumeAvgIOPS` (Ops/s), `VolumeAvgThroughput` (KiB/s), `VolumeAvgReadLatency`, `VolumeAvgWriteLatency` | `VolumeId` AND `InstanceId`. Nitro instances only |\\n| AWS/EBS | `VolumeReadOps`, `VolumeWriteOps`, `VolumeReadBytes`, `VolumeWriteBytes`, `VolumeTotalReadTime`, `VolumeTotalWriteTime`, `VolumeQueueLength`, `VolumeIdleTime`, `BurstBalance`, `VolumeThroughputPercentage` (Provisioned IOPS SSD only) | `VolumeId` |\\n| AWS/EC2 | `EBSIOBalance%`, `EBSByteBalance%`, `EBSReadOps`, `EBSWriteOps`, `EBSReadBytes`, `EBSWriteBytes` | `InstanceId` |\\n\\nMetric math from the Amazon CloudWatch metrics page for Amazon EBS. Use `Sum` statistics for ops, bytes and time.\\n\\n- IOPS = Sum(`VolumeReadOps` + `VolumeWriteOps`) / period in seconds\\n- MiB/s = Sum(`VolumeReadBytes` + `VolumeWriteBytes`) / period in seconds / 1,048,576\\n- Average latency per operation = `VolumeTotalReadTime` / `VolumeReadOps` (and the write equivalent)\\n- Idle percentage = Sum(`VolumeIdleTime`) / period in seconds x 100\\n- MiB/s from `VolumeAvgThroughput` = value in KiB/s / 1,024\\n\\nWhat a 1-minute average hides: sub-minute peaks can reach a limit while the minute average looks below it (micro-bursting). When latency or queue length rises while the average sits below the limit, say that headroom is not proven instead of claiming it.\\n\\n`EBSIOBalance%` and `EBSByteBalance%` are published only for some instance sizes (generally 4xlarge and smaller) that can burst. If they are absent, the instance does not publish them. That is not a fault.\\n\\n## Errors and fallbacks\\n\\n| What happens | What it means | What to do |\\n|---|---|---|\\n| `AccessDenied` on any call | The role cannot read that data | Name the exact API in Gaps. Continue with the rest |\\n| A read call is held behind an operator-approval gate (for example `dlm:GetLifecyclePolicies` or `rbin:ListRules`) | The Agent Space treats it as an action | Report it as a Gap and say which conclusion stays unconfirmed. Never ask the operator to bypass the gate |\\n| No `VolumeAvg*` data | The instance is not Nitro, or the `InstanceId` dimension is missing | Add `InstanceId`. If still empty, use the Sum-based math above |\\n| `EBSIOBalance%` absent | The instance size does not publish it | Compare the summed IOPS and MiB/s of all attached volumes to the `DescribeInstanceTypes` baseline |\\n| `DescribeInstanceTypes` values in MB/s | The API reports instance throughput in MB/s (bandwidth in Mbps) | Convert to MiB/s before comparing (1 MB/s = 1,000,000 bytes/s; 1 MiB/s = 1,048,576 bytes/s) |\\n| AWS CloudTrail optional lookup denied or empty | No access, or the event is outside retention | Use `DescribeVolumesModifications` for the change record. It is not bound by AWS CloudTrail retention |\\n| No metric data for a volume | The volume is new, detached, or the window is wrong | Check `DescribeVolumes` state and attachment times, widen the window, report the Gap |\\n\\n## Sources\\n\\n- Amazon CloudWatch metrics for Amazon EBS: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/using_cloudwatch_ebs.html\\n- Instance metrics, including `EBSIOBalance%` and `EBSByteBalance%`: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/viewing_metrics_with_cloudwatch.html\\n- Amazon EBS-optimized instances (baseline and maximum, MB/s): https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/ebs-optimized.html\\n- Monitoring volume modifications: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/monitoring-volume-modifications.html\\n- AWS FIS actions: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/fis/latest/userguide/fis-actions-reference.html\\n'}]", "status": "success", "type": "tool_result"}], "created_at": null}

{"id": "20547bb9-54d8-457a-9b44-7fb538f2cb67", "role": "user", "content": [{"id": "tooluse_SXOMfbWGk3A0uJr4SltQuR", "content": "[{'text': '# Troubleshoot: Amazon EBS cost and billing\\n\\n## When this path applies\\n\\n- \"Why did my EBS bill go up?\", unexplained Amazon EBS charges, a cost forecast\\n- Idle, unattached or over-provisioned volumes\\n- Snapshot cost growth, Recycle Bin retention cost\\n- Questions about the Amazon EBS pricing model\\n\\n## Procedure\\n\\n1. **Get the cost trend.** AWS Cost Explorer `GetCostAndUsage`, monthly for the last several months and daily for the month that changed, grouped by `USAGE_TYPE`. Amazon EBS charges appear under the \"EC2 - Other\" service in Cost Explorer; confirm this with `GetDimensionValues` for `SERVICE` in the account.\\n2. **List the account\\'s usage types.** `GetDimensionValues` for `USAGE_TYPE` in the period. Do not trust a hardcoded list. Classify each Amazon EBS usage type by its name:\\n   - volume storage (names containing `VolumeUsage`)\\n   - provisioned IOPS (names containing `IOPS`)\\n   - provisioned throughput (names containing `Throughput`)\\n   - snapshots (names containing `Snapshot`)\\n3. **Break the change into components.** Report the change in storage, provisioned IOPS above the included baseline, provisioned throughput above the included baseline, and snapshots, using the account\\'s own Cost Explorer amounts. These include the account\\'s discounts and pricing agreements, so never replace them with list prices.\\n4. **Explain the gp3 model when gp3 is involved.** gp3 includes 3,000 IOPS and 125 MiB/s at any size. Only IOPS above 3,000 and throughput above 125 MiB/s are billed as provisioned performance. Link the pricing page; do not type a price.\\n5. **Find what changed.**\\n   - `DescribeVolumesModifications` for every volume: original and target size, type, IOPS and throughput, with start time. This record is not bound by AWS CloudTrail retention.\\n   - `DescribeVolumes` `CreateTime` for new volumes, and `status=available` for unattached volumes.\\n   - Volume type changes (for example gp2 to gp3, or gp3 to io2) from the modification record.\\n   - Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager `GetLifecyclePolicies` and AWS Backup `ListBackupPlans` for policies that create or retain snapshots.\\n   - Recycle Bin `ListRules`: resources in Recycle Bin are still billed during retention.\\n   - AWS CloudTrail `LookupEvents` is optional, only if available, to find who made a change. If it is denied or empty, write a Gap and continue.\\n6. **Right-sizing check** for volumes with provisioned performance.\\n   - Measured IOPS and MiB/s over a representative window (`VolumeAvgIOPS` / `VolumeAvgThroughput` with `VolumeId` and `InstanceId`, or the Sum-based math in [data-collection.md](data-collection.md)) against provisioned values.\\n   - Provisioned performance above what the attached instance\\'s EBS baseline can deliver.\\n   - AWS Compute Optimizer `GetEBSVolumeRecommendations` if enabled (optional).\\n7. **Separate findings.** Posture issues seen during the check (unencrypted volumes, untagged volumes, no backup coverage, no alarms) go under Separate findings with a suggestion to run Review mode ([review-operational.md](review-operational.md)).\\n\\n## Decision rules\\n\\n- The Answer names the component and the resource that drove the change, with the date from the modification record or `CreateTime`.\\n- Snapshot savings are an upper bound because snapshots are incremental.\\n- A volume with provisioned performance far above measured demand or above the instance baseline is a right-sizing candidate. Do not apply a fixed percentage rule; show the measured and provisioned values and let the operator decide.\\n\\n## What to report\\n\\nThe verdict template in [finding-logic.md](finding-logic.md). Evidence is a table of components (storage, IOPS, throughput, snapshots) with the account\\'s own amounts for the two periods compared, and the change records that explain each. Binding layer is \"Not applicable\". Recommendation lists right-sizing, deletion or type-change proposals with exact parameters and cost direction.\\n\\n## Safety rules\\n\\n- This path is read-only.\\n- Deleting volumes or snapshots, changing volume types and lowering IOPS or throughput are proposals for a directed action approved on the approval card. Each proposal names the volume, the exact parameters, the cost direction and the rollback. For deletions, recommend a snapshot first and say whether a Recycle Bin rule will catch it.\\n- Never type a price. Use the account\\'s Cost Explorer amounts and link the pricing page.\\n\\n## Sources\\n\\n- Amazon EBS pricing: https://aws.amazon.com/ebs/pricing/\\n- gp3 included performance: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/general-purpose.html\\n- Monitoring volume modifications: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/monitoring-volume-modifications.html\\n- Snapshots (incremental): https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/ebs-snapshots.html\\n- Recycle Bin: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/recycle-bin.html\\n- Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/snapshot-lifecycle.html\\n- AWS Backup resource assignment: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/aws-backup/latest/devguide/assigning-resources.html\\n'}]", "status": "success", "type": "tool_result"}, {"id": "tooluse_lbTZSTlhkwtV9trmreL5M7", "content": "[{'text': '# Data collection: read-only APIs, metric math, errors and fallbacks\\n\\nLoad this file on every request. Every value in a verdict or a review comes from one of these calls. Tags are used for naming only, never as the source of a configuration value.\\n\\n## Read-only API allowlist\\n\\n| Service | APIs |\\n|---|---|\\n| Amazon EC2 | `DescribeVolumes`, `DescribeVolumeStatus`, `DescribeVolumesModifications`, `DescribeVolumeAttribute`, `DescribeInstances`, `DescribeInstanceTypes`, `DescribeInstanceAttribute`, `DescribeSnapshots`, `DescribeSnapshotAttribute`, `DescribeImages`, `DescribeFastSnapshotRestores`, `GetEbsEncryptionByDefault`, `GetEbsDefaultKmsKeyId`, `GetSnapshotBlockPublicAccessState`, `DescribeLockedSnapshots` |\\n| Amazon CloudWatch | `DescribeAlarms`, `DescribeAlarmHistory`, `GetMetricData`, `ListMetrics` |\\n| Service Quotas | `ListServiceQuotas`, `GetServiceQuota`, `GetAWSDefaultServiceQuota`, `ListRequestedServiceQuotaChangeHistoryByQuota` |\\n| Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager | `GetLifecyclePolicies`, `GetLifecyclePolicy` |\\n| Recycle Bin | `ListRules`, `GetRule` |\\n| AWS Backup | `ListBackupPlans`, `ListBackupSelections`, `GetBackupSelection`, `ListRecoveryPointsByResource` (always with `ManagedByAWSBackupOnly` set to true; without it the call also returns snapshots AWS Backup did not create), `ListProtectedResources` |\\n| AWS KMS | `DescribeKey`, `GetKeyPolicy`, `ListGrants` |\\n| AWS Cost Explorer | `GetCostAndUsage`, `GetDimensionValues` |\\n| AWS FIS | `ListExperiments`, `GetExperiment` |\\n| AWS Health | `DescribeEvents` |\\n| AWS Compute Optimizer (optional) | `GetEBSVolumeRecommendations` |\\n| AWS CloudTrail (optional) | `LookupEvents`. Use `Sum` statistics for ops, bytes and time.\\n\\n- IOPS = Sum(`VolumeReadOps` + `VolumeWriteOps`) / period in seconds\\n- MiB/s = Sum(`VolumeReadBytes` + `VolumeWriteBytes`) / period in seconds / 1,048,576\\n- Average latency per operation = `VolumeTotalReadTime` / `VolumeReadOps` (and the write equivalent)\\n- Idle percentage = Sum(`VolumeIdleTime`) / period in seconds x 100\\n- MiB/s from `VolumeAvgThroughput` = value in KiB/s / 1,024\\n\\nWhat a 1-minute average hides: sub-minute peaks can reach a limit while the minute average looks below it (micro-bursting). When latency or queue length rises while the average sits below the limit, say that headroom is not proven instead of claiming it.\\n\\n`EBSIOBalance%` and `EBSByteBalance%` are published only for some instance sizes (generally 4xlarge and smaller) that can burst. It is not bound by AWS CloudTrail retention |\\n| No metric data for a volume | The volume is new, detached, or the window is wrong | Check `DescribeVolumes` state and attachment times, widen the window, report the Gap |\\n\\n## Sources\\n\\n- Amazon CloudWatch metrics for Amazon EBS: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/using_cloudwatch_ebs.html\\n- Instance metrics, including `EBSIOBalance%` and `EBSByteBalance%`: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/viewing_metrics_with_cloudwatch.html\\n- Amazon EBS-optimized instances (baseline and maximum, MB/s): https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/ebs-optimized.html\\n- Monitoring volume modifications: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/monitoring-volume-modifications.html\\n- AWS FIS actions: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/fis/latest/userguide/fis-actions-reference.html\\n'}]", "status": "success", "type": "tool_result"}, {"id": "tooluse_WfIzlkfdS1WLfAoL3jf2ub", "content": "[{'text': '# Finding logic: verdict template, binding layer, escalation, review ratings\\n\\n## Troubleshoot verdict template\\n\\nEvery troubleshoot answer uses these six headings in this order.\\n\\n1. **Answer.** The question the user asked, answered first in one or two sentences. For example \"Not stuck. The modification is in `optimizing`, which already applies the new IOPS.\"\\n2. **Evidence.** The values that support the answer, each with units and the time window (for example \"average `<value>` IOPS, `<start>` to `<end>` UTC\"). Throughput in MiB/s.\\n3. **Binding layer.** One of: Volume, Instance, Burst credits, Quota, Not EBS, AWS-side impairment, Not applicable.\\n4. **Recommendation.** Exact parameters (volume ID, dimension, target value, how the target was computed), or \"No change\". Mutating steps are proposals for a directed action.\\n5. **Separate findings.** Other true facts, labelled so they never change the Answer. For example a modification that succeeded on a volume whose instance caps delivered IOPS: the cap goes here, never as \"the modification failed\".\\n6. **Gaps.** What could not be checked and why (API denied, approval gate, metric absent).\\n\\n## Binding-layer decision tree\\n\\nWork through it in order. Use measured values and the limits read from the APIs. Do not use fixed percentage triggers.\\n\\n1. Is the summed IOPS or MiB/s of all attached volumes flat at the instance EBS baseline, or are `EBSIOBalance%` / `EBSByteBalance%` draining or at 0?\\n   - Yes: **Instance**. Say \"the volume has headroom; raising volume IOPS will not help; change the instance type\". If a volume is also flat at its own limit, report both and fix the instance first, because volume changes cannot deliver above the instance ceiling.\\n2. Is the instance healthy and one volume flat at its own provisioned limit on the dimension its type is judged by?\\n   - Yes: **Volume**.\\n3. Is a gp2, st1 or sc1 volume\\'s `BurstBalance` draining or at 0?\\n   - Yes: **Burst credits**.\\n4. Did an operation fail on a quota (error text names a limit)?\\n   - Yes: **Quota**. Use the Capacity and quota headroom section of [review-operational.md](review-operational.md).\\n5. Are all layers below their limits, latency at the volume\\'s normal level, and queue length low?\\n   - Yes: **Not EBS**. Check CPU, memory, network and the application.\\n6. Are all layers below their limits but latency and `VolumeQueueLength` up while IOPS and throughput collapse?\\n   - Yes: **AWS-side impairment** (or injected latency). The report layout is in [review-report-format.md](review-report-format.md).\\n\\n## Sources\\n\\n- Volume status checks: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/monitoring-volume-status.html\\n- Detaching volumes: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/ebs-detaching-volume.html\\n- Monitoring volume modifications: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/monitoring-volume-modifications.html\\n- Modification duration (more than 24 hours in some cases): https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/ebs-modify-volume.html and https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/monitoring-volume-modifications.html\\n- Amazon EBS performance: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/ebs-performance.html\\n- Published S3 skill rating scale (format only): https://github.com/aws/tools-for-devops-agent\\n'}]", "status": "success", "type": "tool_result"}, {"id": "tooluse_mi2IGRUs0JULwKrzlHmMWq", "content": "[{'text': '# Amazon EBS service rules and quirks\\n\\nLoad this file for any statement about how Amazon EBS behaves. Per-type limits are in [metrics-thresholds.md](metrics-thresholds.md).\\n\\n## Elastic Volumes rules\\n\\n- You can make up to 4 modifications to a volume in a rolling 24-hour period. There is no fixed waiting period between modifications; the next one is allowed once the previous one completes (January 2026 change).\\n- Size can only increase. It cannot be reduced. To get a smaller volume, create a new volume and copy the data.\\n- A modification request cannot be cancelled after it is submitted.\\n- States are `modifying`, then `optimizing`, then `completed` (or `failed`). In `optimizing` the new configuration already applies, and performance is between the source and the target. The modification completes on its own.\\n- Duration is best effort. The Amazon EBS User Guide says a 1 TiB volume typically takes up to about six hours to modify, and some performance changes take more than 24 hours, for example when the volume is not fully initialized.\\n- After a size increase, the operating system must extend the partition and the file system. The agent gives the commands; the operator runs them.\\n- Read the requirements page before proposing a change on an older instance, or on a volume with an MBR partition (2 TiB limit).\\n\\n## Instance EBS layer\\n\\n- All volumes attached to an instance share the instance\\'s EBS bandwidth, IOPS and throughput. Sum the measured values across all attached volumes, including the root volume.\\n- Size any target within the instance\\'s EBS baseline from `DescribeInstanceTypes`, not its burst maximum.\\n- `DescribeInstanceTypes` reports throughput in MB/s at 128 KiB I/O and IOPS at 16 KiB I/O. Convert MB/s to MiB/s before comparing with volume throughput.\\n- Some smaller instance sizes burst above the baseline for a limited time and publish `EBSIOBalance%` and `EBSByteBalance%`. When those balances drain or reach 0, the instance drops to its baseline.\\n\\n## Quotas\\n\\n- Amazon EBS quotas are per Region. Check each Region the user works in.\\n- Discover quota codes by name with `ListServiceQuotas --service-code ebs`. Never hardcode quota codes.\\n- Read defaults from the Amazon EBS quotas page. For example, the default for snapshots per Region is 100,000 and it is adjustable.\\n- The io2 regional IOPS quota is separate from the per-volume maximum. A request within the per-volume maximum can still fail on the regional quota. Existing io2 volumes already consume part of that quota.\\n- Adjustable quotas are raised through Service Quotas. Quotas that are not adjustable need an AWS Support case.\\n\\n## Snapshots\\n\\n- Snapshots are incremental. Deleting a snapshot might not reduce storage cost, because later snapshots can reference its blocks. Any savings figure is an upper bound.\\n- You cannot delete a snapshot that is the root device snapshot of a registered AMI, even if the AMI is deprecated or disabled. Deregister the AMI first, and only if it is no longer needed.\\n- Snapshots created by AWS Backup are managed in AWS Backup, not with Amazon EC2 delete calls.\\n- Identify Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager snapshots by `aws:dlm:*` tags, never by the snapshot name or description. A snapshot can be named like a DLM snapshot and still have no `aws:dlm:*` tags.\\n- Target tags for Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager policies are case sensitive.\\n- Recycle Bin rules decide whether a deleted snapshot can be recovered. With no matching rule, deletion is permanent.\\n\\n## Quirks that change answers\\n\\n| Quirk | Rule |\\n|---|---|\\n| `VolumeThroughputPercentage` on io1/io2 | Reports the percentage of provisioned IOPS delivered.
